transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling really awful about myself. I know that sounds kind of vague, sorry. It’s like I can’t stop thinking that I’m a danger or a disappointment… especially after this near-miss at work. I keep taking it as proof that maybe I’m not meant to be a nurse, and… I don’t know, like everyone would be better off without me. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?

I… not exactly killing myself, no. I mean, I don’t have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that.

But… I do keep having thoughts like it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or if I could disappear so I wouldn’t mess anything up again. I know that probably sounds bad. I’m sorry.
Did these feelings start after the near-miss at work?

Not just after that, no… I mean, the near-miss made it feel a lot worse and harder to ignore, but I think it’s been going on for a while.

Probably about a year and a couple months? Since after I graduated high school and started taking college classes and working full-time at the clinic. I should’ve handled it better, I know, but that’s when it kind of started.
Do these feelings seem mainly connected to the stress of school and working full-time?

I think that’s when it started, yeah… after I graduated high school and started trying to do college classes while working full-time at the clinic. It’s been about a year and two months now, I guess.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just blaming stress or anything, but that was the time it began getting really hard. Does that make sense?
For at least two weeks at a time, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try not to show it, especially at work, because I know I’m supposed to be professional.

But most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Even when I’m smiling at patients in Spanish or trying to act normal at the clinic, I feel like I’m just… barely holding myself together. Is that what you mean?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think I have. I mean, I still tell myself I’ll do things, like go for a jog or knit a little, or cook something, read after class… stuff that used to help me clear my head.

But lately I just end up sitting on my bed in my scrubs, and I can’t really make myself care enough to start. I know that sounds kind of lazy, but it doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it, if that makes sense.
Before this past year, had you ever gone through another period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed like this most days?

I don’t think so… not like this.

I mean, I had normal bad weeks before, like with school or being tired, but I don’t remember a whole stretch where it was most days for two weeks or more. At least, not that I would’ve called the same as this. Is that an okay way to answer?
Have you noticed a big change in your appetite?

Um… maybe a little. I don’t think I’m doing it on purpose or anything.

I just kind of forget to eat until really late in the day, and then I’ll realize and have, like, crackers or coffee because it’s easy. I know that’s probably not great. My work pants have been feeling looser too, even though I’m not trying to lose weight. Is that the kind of change you mean?
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I mean, I do sleep some, so it’s not like I’m up all night every night.

But when I get in bed, my brain just keeps going over charts and medication calculations, like I’m checking them again in my head. And then when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up before my alarm feeling already worn out, and kind of scared I missed something. Is that… is that what you mean by trouble sleeping?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’m still getting things done, mostly, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I’ll read the same medication order or a lecture slide over and over, and it just doesn’t… stick. My brain feels kind of foggy. Even small things, like deciding what to chart first, can make me freeze for a minute. Is that the kind of concentration problem you’re asking about?
Even on days when work and school are relatively calm, do you still feel depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, even when nothing really bad happens that day, I still wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest.

I can smile at patients and, you know, speak Spanish with them and try to seem normal at the clinic, so I don’t think people can always tell. But inside it feels like I’m barely keeping it together. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?

Maybe… yeah, a little. I don’t think it’s dramatic or anything, but people at the clinic have asked if I’m tired because I’m moving kind of slower getting supplies.

And sometimes when someone asks me even a simple question, it takes me a few seconds to answer, like I have to catch up. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. Is that what you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

Um… I don’t think so? Not about a lot of different things, at least.

I mean, I worry some, like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say it’s excessive or all over the place. It’s more that I get stuck in my head sometimes. But I’m not sure if that counts as worrying the way you mean.
Have these feelings made it hard for you to do your job, keep up with school, or manage things at home?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not functioning at all, because I am still showing up.

But I’ve definitely fallen behind in my nursing prereqs, more than I want to admit. And at work, I’ve started asking coworkers to double-check things I used to feel totally confident doing on my own. It’s embarrassing… like I’m scared to take on normal clinic responsibilities now in case I mess something up.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you been feeling worthless, or blaming yourself a lot for things that aren’t really your fault?

Yeah… I guess I have been. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but it’s been hard to stop thinking I’m… like, a danger or a disappointment.

That near-miss at work just keeps playing in my head, and I keep taking it as proof that maybe I’m not meant to be a nurse. Like everyone would be better off if I wasn’t there making things harder or risky. I know that probably sounds extreme… I’m sorry. Is that the kind of blaming yourself you mean?
